question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
7\sqrt[6]{4-25x}-21=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7\sqrt[6]{4-25x}-21 & =0 \\ 7\sqrt[6]{4-25x} & =21 \\ \sqrt[6]{4-25x} & =3 \\ {(\sqrt[6]{4-25x})}^{6} & ={3}^{6} \\ 4-25x & =729 \\ -25x & =725 \\ x & =-29\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}7\sqrt[6]{4-25\cdot (-29)}-21 & =0 \\ 7\sqrt[6]{729}-21 & =0 \\ 7\cdot 3-21 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=-29.$
